note: Sun 23 Aug 2026, ~07:02 SGT — weekend run, before Monday's Asia open (SGX/HKEX 09:00-09:30 SGT 24 Aug). US/HK/SG/JP/KR all closed since Friday 21 Aug; nothing new to bake for equities/breadth/regional-flow data since Saturday's edition — this run's incremental work is a Sat/Sun news sweep (see news.json) plus re-verification. WEEKEND DEVELOPMENTS: (1) Iran conflict escalated further Sat 22 Aug — Trump said Iran could be bombed 'a little bit more' as the US pivots to an economic crackdown, a senior IRGC-linked figure vowed Tehran 'will not submit', and the White House/Treasury are set to detail the 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran's trading partners on Monday 24 Aug; oil (Brent $94.39, WTI $87.06, Fri settle, both +0.65%/+0.26% and up ~6% on the week) is pricing this in ahead of Monday. (2) Crypto kept running through the weekend on continued ETF-inflow and short-squeeze momentum: BTC's Friday close was $78,335.19 (+7.26%, best weekly performance since 2024, spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $606mn Fri — the largest daily inflow since May, 83% into IBIT), before pulling back intraday to a Saturday level of ~$77,012 (-1.7% from Friday's close; per .prices.json, a LIVE LEVEL not a close). ETH ran to $2,515 (+8.1% Fri) and XRP was the standout at +14.6% to $1.45. (3) Gold/silver/COMEX are shut over the weekend (no new close); Friday's GC=F settle was $4,624.10 (+2.39%) and GLD $423.36 (+1.95%), both still near the 3-month high flagged Friday. Equity Fear & Greed is inferred at 55/Greed (up from Thursday's Neutral, ~50) based on convergent secondary trackers, given CNN's own page again returned HTTP 451 on direct fetch this run.

flows.narrative: The week through 19 Aug showed a decisive rotation into safe-haven/defensive assets: money-market/cash funds drew the largest inflow ($25.4bn), bonds $23.8bn, and gold $6.3bn — its biggest weekly inflow since January 2026 — as BofA's Michael Hartnett reiterated a 'long gold, short USD' stance and flagged his Bull & Bear Indicator at an elevated 9.3, just shy of 'extreme bullish'. Equities still drew a net $16.1bn but this was a slowdown versus prior weeks, consistent with the tech-led deleveraging that hit semis hardest in the Aug 19 rout. Nothing in this release has changed since Saturday's edition; the next print (Fri 28 Aug) will be the first to capture the weekend's Iran-sanctions and crypto-rally headlines.
